title: Docs (three-layer model) + terminal scope-isolation / injection / dynamic-listing verification (runs last)

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: Terminal story: owns the epic-wide security proof (injection, cross-tenant, no-column-leak, dynamic-listing correctness) and the docs. Depends on all leaves; runs last.

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; mirrors epic_28/epic_29 terminal-verification pattern. loopctl is agent-native (no web UI).
background.includes: Each prior story asserts its slice; this story proves the generic path end-to-end (define -> list -> query) across API + MCP, proves the security properties epic-wide, and writes docs/context-retriever.md including the three-layer model (Knowledge Wiki vs Agent Memory vs Context Retriever) the Cole Medin comparison clarified.

story.i_want_to: run one end-to-end pass that defines an entity, lists its generated tools, and queries it via API and MCP, while proving no injection, no cross-tenant read, and no undeclared-column leak, and document the three-layer model
story.so_that: the context-retriever pillar ships proven-safe and clearly distinguished from the knowledge wiki and agent memory

rationale: The context retriever lets a model's output drive database queries across tenants, so its safety properties must be proven across the whole define->list->execute path, not just per unit. A single terminal security verification plus authoritative docs (the three-layer mental model) turns the merged stories into a trustworthy, teachable capability.

acceptance_criteria.description: docs/context-retriever.md is written: the entity->generator->executor architecture, the security model (allowlist, parameterization, tenant/role scoping, pagination cap, no model SQL), and the THREE-LAYER model — Knowledge Wiki (curated) vs Agent Memory (scoped, auto-accumulated) vs Context Retriever (governed structured-data access). States loopctl is agent-native (no web UI); entity management is via API/MCP.

README.md, CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md (agent guidance: when to use retrieve_* vs knowledge_* vs memory_*), CHANGELOG.md updated; endpoints render at /swaggerui. The #309 'reconcile docs/cole-medin-self-evolving-wiki.md' item is noted as already satisfied (removed in PR #310; content in KB hub fb9abd73).

An end-to-end integration test: define an entity via API -> the generated tool appears in MCP ListTools -> a query via both POST /retrieve and the MCP generated tool returns the same tenant-scoped results.

A terminal SECURITY suite proves epic-wide: (a) an injection payload in a filter value matches literally (no SQL execution); (b) a non-allowlisted field is rejected on every surface; (c) cross-tenant define/list/query isolation holds via context, API, and MCP; (d) no undeclared column leaks in results.

test_cases.name: end-to-end define -> ListTools -> query (API + MCP) agree
steps: POST /retrieve/project and call the MCP generated tool
expected_results: the generated tool is listed; API + MCP queries return the same tenant-scoped result set

test_cases.name: terminal security: injection + non-allowlist + cross-tenant + no-leak
preconditions: two tenants each with entities + rows; an injection value; a non-allowlisted field; an entity declaring a field subset
steps: attempt cross-tenant list/query via API + MCP
expected_results: injection matches literally/no SQL; non-allowlist rejected everywhere; no cross-tenant data on any surface; only declared fields returned

technical_notes: Model on epic_28 US-28.5 / epic_29 US-29.6 terminal-verification pattern: depends on all leaves, runs last.
docs/context-retriever.md is authoritative for the three-layer model; keep it short and decision-oriented.
Tests reuse Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 and real project/story rows across two tenants.
